rows.text: returns at once when `edx` is 0; otherwise, for `edx` destination records of stride 0x130 starting at `rcx`, skips a null destination and else copies 0x100 bytes from `r8` to it, calls `0019D8D0(dest+0x100, r8+0x100)` and copies qword `+0x120` and byte `+0x128` from `r8`; the same source `r8` is used for every record
copies 0x100 bytes from `rdx` to `rcx` in two 0x80-byte passes, calls `0019D8D0(rcx+0x100, rdx+0x100)`, copies qword `+0x120` and byte `+0x128` from `rdx` to `rcx` and returns `rcx`

calls `001AB350(rcx, qword [rcx], qword [rcx+8])`, then when qword `[rcx]` is non-null releases it through virtual slot `+0x18` of the object at `rcx+0x18` with size ((qword `+0x10` minus qword `+0`) / 0x30, signed) * 0x30

when qword `rcx+8` is below qword `rcx+0x10` (unsigned), advances qword `rcx+8` by 0x30 and, if the old value is non-null, copies dword `[rdx]` and word `rdx+4` into it, calls `0019D8D0(old+8, rdx+8)` and copies byte `rdx+0x28` to `old+0x28`; otherwise calls `001AB8A0(rcx, qword rcx+8, rdx)`

walks the list from qword `rcx+0x80` until it reaches `rcx+0x78`, calling for each node `00185A90(00189120(), the address loaded at 001B6AA0, node qword +0x20)` and stepping with `0016D6D0(node)`; then walks the chain from qword `rcx+0x88` (next at `+8`) calling `00220390(rcx+0x70, link qword +0)` and releasing each link through virtual slot `+0x18` of the object at `rcx+0xa0` with size 0x28; finally points qwords `rcx+0x80` and `rcx+0x78` at `rcx+0x78`, zeroes qword `+0x88`, byte `+0x90` and dword `+0x98`, and returns 1 when dword `+0x60` is 0, else 0

notes: 001B6A70 passes a rip-relative address (lea at 001B6AA0) that lies past this body's extent; it is described by its load site rather than written, since it may be another function or data. The pack header says 5 bodies.
